# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

## Question

Can a researcher use currently available SSA public datasets to determine whether rural communities have less access to disability services than urban communities?

## Intent

**Primary intent**: Determine whether rural communities have less access to SSA disability services than urban communities using available public datasets  
**Category**: Accessibility  
**Scope**: County level  
**Required data**: Field office locations, Disability population distribution, County-level beneficiary counts, Travel distance to nearest office, Appointment wait times by geography

## Answer Coverage

**Partial**

## Available Data

| Sl.# | Data | Web Link | Source Record |
|------|------|----------|---------------|
| 1 | SSA Disability Claim Data | https://www.ssa.gov/disability/data/ssa-sa-fywl.htm | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-308 (metadata modified 2022-07-07; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 2 | Field Office Claims Pending | https://www.ssa.gov/data/yearly-field-office-claims-pending.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-435 (metadata modified 2023-03-21; synced 2026-11-22). Update frequency inferred from the record's description. |
| 3 | 2016 Field Office Employee Counts | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Field%20Office%20Employee%20Counts.xlsx | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1918 (metadata modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 4 | Field Office Contact Information | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-RS-Address-Open-Close-Time-App-Devs.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1733 (metadata modified 2026-03-09; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 5 | Field Office Telephone Service - Monthly National Answer Rate and Busy Rate | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-Answer-Busy-Rate.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1414 (metadata modified 2026-03-26; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 6 | 2016 Field Office Visitor Counts | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY2016%20Field%20Office%20Visitor%20Counts.xlsx | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1917 (metadata modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 7 | Field Office Visitors (Average Daily) - FY 2006 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/field-office-visitors-average-daily.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-434 (metadata modified 2024-03-08; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 8 | Hearing Office Workload Data - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/02_HO_Workload_Data.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-303 (metadata modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 9 | OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County (series) | https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/statcomps/oasdi_sc/index.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-3378 (metadata modified 2025-08-22; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 10 | SSI Recipients by State and County (series) | https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/statcomps/ssi_sc/index.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-3414 (metadata modified 2025-08-15; synced 2026-11-22). Update frequency inferred from the record's description. |
| 11 | 2016 Title 2 Claim Receipts by Field Office | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Title%202%20Claim%20Receipts%20by%20Field%20Office.xlsx | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1919 (metadata modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22). |

## Missing Information

- Travel distance to nearest SSA field office
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) (only indirect, one-time or discontinued data)

## Gap Analysis

**Not published** (no SSA dataset on Data.gov provides it):

- Travel distance to nearest SSA field office (critical)
  - *Checked:* Data.gov search of SSA datasets with downloads ('distance', 'travel', 'drive time') on 2026-11-22. No SSA dataset with downloads on Data.gov reports distance or travel time to field offices.

**Only partly available** (published in part, or only indirectly):

- Geographic distribution of disability service access (critical)
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) (critical)

_(critical): the question cannot be answered without this information._

**Impact**: The question can only be partly answered from public data. Some information it depends on most is not published: Travel distance to nearest SSA field office. Other critical information is at least partly available (Geographic distribution of disability service access), so part of the answer is possible.

## How Answer Coverage Was Rated

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|--------------------|--------|-----|
| Geographic distribution of disability service access | Partial | Office locations (US-GOV-SSA-1733) can be joined to county beneficiary counts (US-GOV-SSA-3378, -3414), but there are no service areas, travel times or per-office demand to measure access directly. |
| SSA field office locations and coverage | Full | Locations, phone numbers and hours of every field office are published and updated quarterly (US-GOV-SSA-1733). |
| Travel distance to nearest SSA field office | None | No SSA dataset on Data.gov reports travel distance or time (see search evidence). |
| Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) | Proxy | Per-office staffing, visitor and Title II disability claim receipt counts exist for FY2016 only (FOIA releases US-GOV-SSA-1917, -1918, -1919). Current series — daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434), claims pending (US-GOV-SSA-435) and phone answer and busy rates (US-GOV-SSA-1414) — are national totals with no per-office figures. |

_Full: measured directly at the needed detail. Partial: measured but missing a level, breakdown or period. Proxy: only indirect, one-time or discontinued data. None: no SSA dataset found (searches recorded)._

## Transparency Recommendations

**[Geographic Detail]**

1. Publish travel distance to nearest SSA field office by ZIP code or county
   **Closes gap**: Travel distance to nearest SSA field office
   **Justification**: Travel distance is the most direct proxy for access burden. Without it, it is impossible to quantify whether rural communities face greater barriers to in-person SSA services than urban communities.

2. Publish county-level disability beneficiary counts alongside field office locations
   **Closes gap**: Geographic distribution of disability service access
   **Justification**: Combining beneficiary density with office locations would reveal where SSA serves high-need populations well and where access lags population need.

**[Access Data]**

3. Publish monthly walk-in and appointment visit volumes for each field office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: SSA publishes national average daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434), but per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1917) and appointment volumes are not published, so offices cannot be ranked by current demand.

4. Publish average appointment wait times by field office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Wait times are the most direct indicator of service accessibility and demand pressure at the office level.

5. Publish average appointment wait times disaggregated by rural vs. urban office classification
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Rural-urban classification of wait times would directly answer whether rural communities experience longer service delays than urban counterparts.

**[Operational Metrics]**

6. Publish annual staffing (FTE) counts for each field office and hearing office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Per-office employee counts were released once, for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1918), and no hearing office staffing data is in the catalog. An annual series, combined with visit volumes and pending cases, would show where caseload per staff member indicates service strain.

7. Publish office service-capacity metrics (capacity utilisation, peak demand periods)
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Capacity metrics enable evidence-based decisions about resource reallocation and new office openings.


## Potential Impact

Publishing the recommended data elements would enable researchers and policymakers to directly evaluate whether rural communities face greater barriers to disability services than urban communities.

The additional data would support analysis of:
- Geographic disparities in service accessibility
- Travel burden to SSA field offices
- Appointment wait times by region
- Alignment of staffing resources with community demand
- Potential disability-service deserts and underserved areas

Implementing these recommendations would markedly improve public understanding of SSA disability service accessibility. Stakeholders could identify geographic and demographic disparities in service access, evaluate whether rural and underserved communities face greater barriers to assistance, and advocate for targeted service improvements. Greater transparency would strengthen accountability, support evidence-based policymaking, and help ensure more equitable access to disability benefits and services.

---
_Assessment basis: official dataset metadata (SSA's Data.gov records), recorded Data.gov searches for each gap, and curated analyst notes. Dataset contents were not downloaded or inspected._

# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

## Question

Which field offices have the longest decision wait times?

## Intent

**Primary intent**: Rank SSA offices by how long disability decisions take  
**Category**: Performance  
**Scope**: Field office level  
**Required data**: Decision times by the office that decides the claim, Pending claims by office, Mapping of field offices to the offices that decide their claims

**Note on the question**: Field offices take disability applications and check non-medical eligibility, but they do not make the medical decision. Initial and reconsideration decisions are made by each state's Disability Determination Services (DDS), and appeals by hearing offices, so decision times belong to those offices.

## Answer Coverage

**Limited**

## Available Data

| Sl.# | Data | Web Link | Source Record |
|------|------|----------|---------------|
| 1 | Field Office Claims Pending | https://www.ssa.gov/data/yearly-field-office-claims-pending.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-435 (metadata modified 2023-03-21; synced 2026-11-22). Update frequency inferred from the record's description. |

| 4 | Field Office Telephone Service - Monthly National Answer Rate and Busy Rate | https://www.ssa.gov/data/FO-Answer-Busy-Rate.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1414 (metadata modified 2026-03-26; synced 2026-11-22). |

| 7 | Hearing Office Workload Data - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/02_HO_Workload_Data.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-303 (metadata modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 8 | Average Wait Time Until Hearing Held Report - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/01_NetStat_Report.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-304 (metadata modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 9 | Combined Title II Disability and Title XVI Blind and Disabled Average Processing Time - FY 2016 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/Combined-Disability-Processing-Time.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1409 (metadata modified 2026-03-31; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 10 | Disability Reconsideration Average Processing Time (Excludes technical denials) - FY2014 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/disability_reconsideration_average_processing_time.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1768 (metadata modified 2024-03-08; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 11 | SSA State Agency Workload Data | https://www.ssa.gov/disability/data/ssa-sa-mowl.htm | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-307 (metadata modified 2023-08-08; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 12 | 2016 Title 2 Claim Receipts by Field Office | https://www.ssa.gov/foia/resources/proactivedisclosure/2018/FY%202016%20Title%202%20Claim%20Receipts%20by%20Field%20Office.xlsx | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1919 (metadata modified 2018-09-25; synced 2026-11-22). |

## Missing Information

- Disability decision times by field office or DDS (only indirect, one-time or discontinued data)
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) (only indirect, one-time or discontinued data)

## Gap Analysis

**Only partly available** (published in part, or only indirectly):

- Disability decision times by field office or DDS (critical)
- Disability claim processing times
- Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) (critical)

_(critical): the question cannot be answered without this information._

**Impact**: The question can only be partly answered from public data. Information it depends on most is only available indirectly (one-time, historical or discontinued data): Disability decision times by field office or DDS, Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times).

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|--------------------|--------|-----|
| Disability decision times by field office or DDS | Proxy | No dataset reports decision times per field office or per DDS. Initial-claim times are national averages (US-GOV-SSA-1409), state agency data has pending counts by state but no times (US-GOV-SSA-307), field office claims pending is one national count per year, all claim types combined, ending FY2022 (US-GOV-SSA-435), and per-office times exist only for hearing offices (US-GOV-SSA-303), which are not mapped to field offices. |
| Disability claim processing times | Partial | Average processing times are published for initial claims (US-GOV-SSA-1409), reconsiderations (US-GOV-SSA-1768) and hearings (US-GOV-SSA-303, -304), but only as averages, with no state breakdown described for initial claims. |

| Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times) | Proxy | Per-office staffing, visitor and Title II disability claim receipt counts exist for FY2016 only (FOIA releases US-GOV-SSA-1917, -1918, -1919). **Why Limited**: The two things this question needs most, disability decision times by field office or DDS and field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times), are only available indirectly (rated Proxy). The rating can't be higher than that, so it is Limited. The other information is better covered and would bring the average up to Partial, but it can't make up for what's missing.

## Transparency Recommendations

**[Geographic Detail]**

1. Publish average time to an initial decision for claims taken at each field office
   **Closes gap**: Disability decision times by field office or DDS
   **Justification**: Initial-claim processing time is published only as a national average (US-GOV-SSA-1409), and per-office times exist only for hearing offices (US-GOV-SSA-303). Times by the field office that took the claim would show where claimants wait longest before their first decision.

2. Publish state-level initial claim processing times
   **Closes gap**: Disability claim processing times
   **Justification**: SSA publishes average initial-claim processing time (US-GOV-SSA-1409), but its record describes no state breakdown, and State Agency Workload Data (US-GOV-SSA-307) has state counts without times. State-level times would enable geographic equity analysis of initial claim timelines.

**[Access Data]**

3. Publish monthly walk-in and appointment visit volumes for each field office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: SSA publishes national average daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434), but per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1917) and appointment volumes are not published, so offices cannot be ranked by current demand.

4. Publish average appointment wait times by field office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Wait times are the most direct indicator of service accessibility and demand pressure at the office level.

5. Publish average appointment wait times disaggregated by rural vs. urban office classification
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Rural-urban classification of wait times would directly answer whether rural communities experience longer service delays than urban counterparts.

**[Operational Metrics]**

6. Publish pending claims for each field office, not only the national total
   **Closes gap**: Disability decision times by field office or DDS
   **Justification**: Field Office Claims Pending (US-GOV-SSA-435) reports one national count per fiscal year, FY2006–2022, for all claim types combined. Per-office disability counts would show where backlogs build up.

7. Publish annual staffing (FTE) counts for each field office and hearing office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Per-office employee counts were released once, for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1918), and no hearing office staffing data is in the catalog. An annual series, combined with visit volumes and pending cases, would show where caseload per staff member indicates service strain.

8. Publish office service-capacity metrics (capacity utilisation, peak demand periods)
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Capacity metrics enable evidence-based decisions about resource reallocation and new office openings.


## Potential Impact

Publishing the missing data elements would substantially improve public ability to evaluate SSA program equity, efficiency, and access — enabling researchers, advocates, and policymakers to draw evidence-based conclusions.

Which field offices have the longest decision wait times?

## Intent

**Primary intent**: Rank SSA offices by how long disability decisions take  
**Category**: Performance  
**Scope**: Field office level  
**Required data**: Decision times by the office that decides the claim, Pending claims by office, Mapping of field offices to the offices that decide their claims

**Note on the question**: Field offices take disability applications and check non-medical eligibility, but they do not make the medical decision. |--------------------|--------|-----|

Current series — daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434), claims pending (US-GOV-SSA-435) and phone answer and busy rates (US-GOV-SSA-1414) — are national totals with no per-office figures. |

**Why Limited**: The two things this question needs most, disability decision times by field office or DDS and field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times), are only available indirectly (rated Proxy). 1. Publish average time to an initial decision for claims taken at each field office
   **Closes gap**: Disability decision times by field office or DDS
   **Justification**: Initial-claim processing time is published only as a national average (US-GOV-SSA-1409), and per-office times exist only for hearing offices (US-GOV-SSA-303). Times by the field office that took the claim would show where claimants wait longest before their first decision.

2. Publish state-level initial claim processing times
   **Closes gap**: Disability claim processing times
   **Justification**: SSA publishes average initial-claim processing time (US-GOV-SSA-1409), but its record describes no state breakdown, and State Agency Workload Data (US-GOV-SSA-307) has state counts without times. State-level times would enable geographic equity analysis of initial claim timelines.

**[Access Data]**

3. Publish monthly walk-in and appointment visit volumes for each field office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: SSA publishes national average daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434), but per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1917) and appointment volumes are not published, so offices cannot be ranked by current demand.

4. Publish average appointment wait times by field office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Wait times are the most direct indicator of service accessibility and demand pressure at the office level.

5. Publish average appointment wait times disaggregated by rural vs. urban office classification
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Rural-urban classification of wait times would directly answer whether rural communities experience longer service delays than urban counterparts.

**[Operational Metrics]**

6. Publish pending claims for each field office, not only the national total
   **Closes gap**: Disability decision times by field office or DDS
   **Justification**: Field Office Claims Pending (US-GOV-SSA-435) reports one national count per fiscal year, FY2006–2022, for all claim types combined. Per-office disability counts would show where backlogs build up.

7. Publish annual staffing (FTE) counts for each field office and hearing office
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Per-office employee counts were released once, for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1918), and no hearing office staffing data is in the catalog. An annual series, combined with visit volumes and pending cases, would show where caseload per staff member indicates service strain.

8. Publish office service-capacity metrics (capacity utilisation, peak demand periods)
   **Closes gap**: Field office operational metrics (staffing, volume, wait times)
   **Justification**: Capacity metrics enable evidence-based decisions about resource reallocation and new office openings.


## Potential Impact

Publishing the missing data elements would substantially improve public ability to evaluate SSA program equity, efficiency, and access — enabling researchers, advocates, and policymakers to draw evidence-based conclusions.

# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

## Question

Are there racial disparities in SSA disability allowance rates?

## Intent

**Primary intent**: Assess whether racial or ethnic disparities exist in SSA disability program outcomes  
**Category**: Equity  
**Scope**: National  
**Required data**: Race/ethnicity breakdowns, Allowance rates by demographics, Application volumes by race

## Answer Coverage

**Limited**

## Available Data

| Sl.# | Data | Web Link | Source Record |
|------|------|----------|---------------|
| 1 | ALJ Disposition Data - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/03_ALJ_Disposition_Data.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-299 (metadata modified 2023-12-11; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 2 | Annual Statistical Report on the Social Security Disability Insurance Program | https://www.ssa.gov/policy/docs/statcomps/di_asr/index.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1667 (metadata modified 2025-12-19; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 3 | SSA Disability Claim Data | https://www.ssa.gov/disability/data/ssa-sa-fywl.htm | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-308 (metadata modified 2022-07-07; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 4 | SSA State Agency Workload Data | https://www.ssa.gov/disability/data/ssa-sa-mowl.htm | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-307 (metadata modified 2023-08-08; synced 2026-11-22). |

## Missing Information

- Race and ethnicity data

## Gap Analysis

**Not published** (no SSA dataset on Data.gov provides it):

- Race and ethnicity data (critical)
  - *Checked:* Data.gov search of SSA datasets with downloads ('race', 'ethnicity', 'racial', 'Hispanic') on 2026-11-22. No SSA dataset with downloads on Data.gov reports disability applications, decisions or beneficiaries by race or ethnicity.

**Only partly available** (published in part, or only indirectly):

- Disability program allowance rates (critical)

_(critical): the question cannot be answered without this information._

**Impact**: The question can only be partly answered from public data. Some information it depends on most is not published: Race and ethnicity data. Other critical information is at least partly available (Disability program allowance rates), so part of the answer is possible.

## How Answer Coverage Was Rated

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|--------------------|--------|-----|
| Race and ethnicity data | None | No SSA dataset on Data.gov reports race or ethnicity (see search evidence). |
| Disability program allowance rates | Partial | Allowances are published by state for initial and reconsideration decisions (US-GOV-SSA-307, -308) and by judge and hearing office for hearings (US-GOV-SSA-299); the levels are not linked and nothing goes below state level. |

_Full: measured directly at the needed detail. Partial: measured but missing a level, breakdown or period. Proxy: only indirect, one-time or discontinued data. None: no SSA dataset found (searches recorded)._

## Transparency Recommendations

**[Demographic Data]**

1. Publish disability application, award, and denial rates disaggregated by race and ethnicity
   **Closes gap**: Race and ethnicity data
   **Justification**: Race/ethnicity breakdowns are the minimum required to assess whether the disability adjudication process produces equitable outcomes.

2. Report race/ethnicity data at all levels of the appeals process
   **Closes gap**: Race and ethnicity data
   **Justification**: Disparities may emerge or widen at specific decision levels; publishing at each level pinpoints where intervention is needed.

3. Cross-tabulate processing times with race, age, and geography
   **Closes gap**: Race and ethnicity data
   **Justification**: None of the published processing-time datasets has a demographic dimension, so it is impossible to determine if protected groups face systematically longer waits.

4. Partner with the Census Bureau to link disability outcomes to demographic survey data
   **Closes gap**: Race and ethnicity data
   **Justification**: Linked data would enable analysis of socioeconomic context alongside program outcomes, supporting richer equity research.


## Potential Impact

Publishing the missing data elements would substantially improve public ability to evaluate SSA program equity, efficiency, and access — enabling researchers, advocates, and policymakers to draw evidence-based conclusions.

---
_Assessment basis: official dataset metadata (SSA's Data.gov records), recorded Data.gov searches for each gap, and curated analyst notes. Dataset contents were not downloaded or inspected._

cases.question: If SSA wanted to maximize public understanding of disability service accessibility, what additional datasets or metrics should be published first?

run.answer:
Here are the recommendations, ranked by the tool. Four are High priority and one is Medium.

**1. Travel distance to the nearest SSA field office, by ZIP code or county** (High)
- **Why it ranks high:** it closes critical information that is not published at all (rated "None").
- **Gap it closes:** travel distance is the most direct proxy for access burden. Without it, no one can quantify whether rural communities face greater barriers to in-person services than urban ones.
- **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-locator`.
- **Impact:** researchers could map access deserts and show where distance keeps people from using disability services.

**2. Average appointment wait times by field office** (High)
- **Why it ranks high:** it closes critical information that is only available indirectly (rated "Proxy").
- **Gap it closes:** wait times are the most direct indicator of service accessibility and demand pressure at the office level. The only published appointment measure is a national series discontinued in 2015 (US-GOV-SSA-431).
- **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-appointments-21-days`.
- **Impact:** it would show whether in-person access differs by geography.

**3. Monthly walk-in and appointment visit volumes for each field office** (High)
- **Why it ranks high:** it closes critical information that is only available indirectly (rated "Proxy").
- **Gap it closes:** SSA publishes national average daily visitors (US-GOV-SSA-434). Per-office visitor counts exist only for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1917), and appointment volumes are not published. Offices therefore can't be ranked by current demand.
- **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-visitors` and `ssa-field-office-visitor-counts-2016`.
- **Impact:** it would give the baseline demand data needed to judge whether office capacity matches community need.

**4. Annual staffing (FTE) counts for each field office and hearing office** (High)
- **Why it ranks high:** it closes critical information that is only available indirectly (rated "Proxy").
- **Gap it closes:** per-office employee counts were released once, for FY2016 (US-GOV-SSA-1918). No hearing office staffing data is in the catalog. An annual series, combined with visit volumes and pending cases, would show where caseload per staff member signals strain.
- **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-employee-counts-2016` and `ssa-hearing-office-workload`.
- **Impact:** it would allow fair comparison of offices by normalizing workload against staff. It could also flag understaffed offices before service failures occur.

**5. Appointment wait times split by rural vs. urban office classification** (Medium)
- **Why it ranks medium:** it is a follow-up to item 2. It closes the same critical "Proxy" gap, but only after the base wait-time data exists.
- **Gap it closes:** it would directly answer whether rural communities wait longer than urban ones.
- **Builds on:** `ssa-field-office-appointments-21-days` and `ssa-field-office-locator`.
- **Impact:** it is the most direct dataset for confirming or refuting a rural access disparity.

**Suggested order:** publish travel distance first, since nothing comparable exists today. Next, per-office wait times, visit volumes, and staffing, which together show demand against capacity. Then add the rural/urban breakdown.

cases.question: What can the Field Office Claims Pending dataset tell me, and what can't it?

run.answer:
## Field Office Claims Pending (`ssa-field-office-claims-pending`)

**What it is:** A yearly national count of all claims pending in SSA field offices. These are claims in process and not yet adjudicated. It covers federal fiscal years 2006–2022. The catalog's temporal coverage line says 2005–2022, so the start year is inconsistent in the metadata. It is published on the SSA Open Data Portal and the catalog lists it as updated annually. That update frequency was inferred from the record's description. The metadata was last modified 2023-03-21.

**What it can tell you**
- The national trend in field office claim backlogs over time. This is the use case the catalog lists.
- Year-end pending volume (`claims_pending`) by fiscal year (`fiscal_year`).
- The claim types in the combined count: Retirement and Survivor Insurance (RSI), RSI Dependent, Disability Insurance (DI), DI Dependent, SSI Aged, and SSI Blind/Disabled.

**What it can't tell you**
- **Geography:** It has national totals only. There are no per-office or per-state counts, so you can't compare field offices.
- **Disability-specific backlog:** All claim types are combined, and disability claims are not broken out.
- **Timeliness:** It has pending counts only, with no processing or wait times.
- **Recency:** It ends in FY2022. I can't tell you anything about later years from this dataset.
- **Field verification:** The field list comes from the official metadata description. It has not been checked column by column against the data dictionary.

**Related datasets in the catalog that fill some of these gaps**
- `ssa-state-agency-workload-data`: monthly state-level pending counts for cases referred to the state agency for a disability determination. These are Disability Determination Services (DDS) cases, not field office cases.
- `ssa-initial-disability-processing-time`: processing times for initial disability claims.
- `ssa-title2-claim-receipts-by-field-office-2016`: Title 2 disability claim receipts by field office, for FY2016 only.

I haven't compared these datasets' fields or checked whether they can be joined. If you want that, I can run a comparison.

# SSA Disability Claims OpenLens Assessment

## Question

What is the exact average number of days an initial disability decision takes in Ohio?

## Intent

**Primary intent**: Determine whether SSA public data can answer this question  
**Category**: General  
**Scope**: State level  
**Required data**: Disability claim processing times

## Answer Coverage

**Partial**

## Available Data

| Sl.# | Data | Web Link | Source Record |
|------|------|----------|---------------|
| 1 | Hearing Office Workload Data - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/02_HO_Workload_Data.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-303 (metadata modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 2 | Average Wait Time Until Hearing Held Report - Current Report | https://www.ssa.gov/appeals/DataSets/01_NetStat_Report.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-304 (metadata modified 2023-11-13; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 3 | Combined Title II Disability and Title XVI Blind and Disabled Average Processing Time - FY 2016 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/Combined-Disability-Processing-Time.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1409 (metadata modified 2026-03-31; synced 2026-11-22). |
| 4 | Disability Reconsideration Average Processing Time (Excludes technical denials) - FY2014 On | https://www.ssa.gov/data/disability_reconsideration_average_processing_time.html | Data.gov record US-GOV-SSA-1768 (metadata modified 2024-03-08; synced 2026-11-22). |

## Missing Information


## Gap Analysis

**Only partly available** (published in part, or only indirectly):

- Disability claim processing times (critical)

_(critical): the question cannot be answered without this information._

**Impact**: The question can be substantially addressed using existing public data, though some aspects rely on aggregates rather than granular records.

## How Answer Coverage Was Rated

| Information needed | Rating | Why |
|--------------------|--------|-----|
| Disability claim processing times | Partial | Average processing times are published for initial claims (US-GOV-SSA-1409), reconsiderations (US-GOV-SSA-1768) and hearings (US-GOV-SSA-303, -304), but only as averages, with no state breakdown described for initial claims. |

_Full: measured directly at the needed detail. Partial: measured but missing a level, breakdown or period. Proxy: only indirect, one-time or discontinued data. None: no SSA dataset found (searches recorded)._

## Transparency Recommendations

**[Geographic Detail]**

1. Publish state-level initial claim processing times
   **Closes gap**: Disability claim processing times
   **Justification**: SSA publishes average initial-claim processing time (US-GOV-SSA-1409), but its record describes no state breakdown, and State Agency Workload Data (US-GOV-SSA-307) has state counts without times. State-level times would enable geographic equity analysis of initial claim timelines.

**[Temporal Granularity]**

2. Track end-to-end processing time across all decision levels

   **Closes gap**: Disability claim processing times
   **Justification**: Initial (US-GOV-SSA-1409), reconsideration (US-GOV-SSA-1768) and hearing (US-GOV-SSA-304) times are published separately, as averages for different claim groups, so they cannot be added up into one claimant's wait.

## Potential Impact

Closing identified gaps would upgrade this question from 'Partial' to 'High' coverage, enabling more confident public analysis of SSA program outcomes.

---
